projects.title: Charm City Kings — HBO Max AR Face Filters
projects.subtitle: XR · AR · Brand Campaign
projects.blurb: A 2-week Spark AR filter campaign for HBO Max's Charm City Kings — 'They call me…' face filters that turn fans into the movie's Baltimore nicknames.
projects.description: For the release of Charm City Kings, HBO Max wanted a way to put fans inside the film's dirt-bike world directly from their phone cameras — no app, no download. The filter turns a marketing beat into something a fan can step into and share.

details.challenge: Standard promo assets ask an audience to sit back; HBO Max wanted something a fan could step inside and share — a moment of participation instead of a passive trailer view.
details.approach: Pulled visual language from the film's dirt-bike and Baltimore street culture, built the AR triggers and overlays in Spark AR and Blender, aligned type and metrics to HBO Max's campaign guidelines, then cross-device tested and submitted to Instagram and Facebook.
details.result: Shipped as an official HBO Max campaign filter for Charm City Kings, live on Instagram and Facebook — turning a passive trailer moment into a participatory brand touchpoint.

projects.title: VisaGenie: AI-Powered Transparency for Global Migration
projects.subtitle: AI · Transparency
projects.blurb: A guided, context-aware AI visa assistant on LangChain + GPT-4 — 95% task completion where static forms left applicants stuck.
projects.description: Visa applications are dense, procedural, and easy to get wrong. VisaGenie turns the process into a guided conversation — an AI assistant, built on LangChain and GPT-4, that asks the right question at the right step and gets applicants to a completed task instead of an abandoned form.

details.challenge: A form doesn't know where you got stuck. Static visa forms and FAQ pages leave applicants to self-diagnose their own confusion. VisaGenie needed to hold context across a multi-step process and respond to wherever the applicant actually was — not a generic script.
details.approach: Mapped the decision tree behind the most common visa paths, structured LangChain prompts to keep GPT-4 on track across multi-turn exchanges, built a chat-first UI with clear progress and context affordances, then iterated prompts against friction points where users dropped off.
details.result: Replaced static forms with a guided, context-aware conversation that held context across the whole process — 95% of applicants completing their visa application to the end.

process.body: Structured LangChain prompts to keep GPT-4 on track across multi-turn exchanges.

process.name: Interface Design

projects.quote: The 95% conversion number mattered less than what it represented: a process that finally met people where their actual confusion was, instead of where a form assumed it would be.

projects.title: Immersive VR Training for Fiber Optic Technicians
projects.subtitle: XR · Enterprise
projects.blurb: VR fiber-optic field training deployed via ArborXR, published on the Meta Quest Store — a fail-safe place to learn splicing and fault diagnosis.
projects.description: Millennium needed field technicians trained on fiber-optic splicing and fault diagnosis without pulling them off paying jobs or risking live customer equipment. The Broken Mile puts them inside a full VR fiber cabinet to run a real troubleshooting job start to finish, as many times as it takes. Deployed via ArborXR and published on the Meta Quest Store.

details.challenge: You can't practice on a live line. Field techs learned splicing by shadowing senior technicians and by trial and error on real customer equipment — expensive when it went wrong, and inconsistent as a way to build judgment.
details.approach: Shadowed field technicians to map the real troubleshooting sequence, then built the fiber cabinet and hand-tracked splice interactions, layered guided and free-play modes so skills build in stages, and packaged the result for ArborXR fleet management.
details.result: Published on the Meta Quest Store and deployed via ArborXR to Millennium's field technician onboarding — replacing live-equipment shadowing with a repeatable, fail-safe practice environment.

notes_wireframe.reflection: Designing for safety-critical, hands-on skills meant the interactive fidelity had to feel like the real tool, not a simplified stand-in — every splice, every fault, had to be trustworthy enough that the learning actually transferred to the field.
